work.title: LAUNCH KIT
work.subtitle: A channel-message launch system
work.scope: Fictional launch copy for Fold Notes, a proposed context-card concept. No product launch, subscriber list, deliverability or results are established.

pages.title: Give the launch one clear job.
pages.lead: Keep the thought beside the note. Fold Notes is a fictional concept for returning to a saved idea without losing the question that made it useful.
pages.body: The launch job is explanation, not a promise of productivity. Invite a reader to inspect the concept and decide whether the proposed interaction fits a real task.
pages.detail: Proposed primary action: review the concept outline. No live destination, product access or release date is supplied.
pages.question: Can a reader explain the concept after one short encounter?

pages.title: Write for a task, not a stereotype.
pages.lead: The intended reader returns to saved material while writing, teaching or planning. The task matters more than an assumed age, title or purchasing habit.
pages.body: Separate a returning reader, a first-time reviewer and an organisational evaluator. These are planning lenses, not researched segments or confirmed demand.
pages.detail: Ask each reader what they need to understand before adapting a headline. Do not infer that task similarity establishes willingness to pay.
pages.question: Which reader question should this channel answer first?

pages.title: Build a message spine.
pages.lead: Save a note with its question. Return to the context before turning it into a new explanation. That is the proposed Fold Notes workflow.
pages.body: Use the same meaning across every channel. Shorter versions may remove detail, but must not upgrade a concept into a released feature or a measured customer benefit.
pages.detail: Lead with the task, explain the interaction, then state the next action. Keep qualifications next to the claim they constrain.
pages.question: Does each adaptation preserve the same capability boundary?

pages.title: Choose headlines by emphasis.
pages.lead: Keep the thought beside the note. A second route is: Return to the question, not just the quotation. A third is: Give a saved idea its context.
pages.body: The three headlines emphasise proximity, retrieval and interpretation. They are editorial alternatives, not the winners of an audience test. Choose against the page purpose before seeking appropriate feedback.
pages.detail: Avoid best, effortless and proven. None is supported by this fictional brief, and each could imply evidence the team does not have.
pages.question: Which headline best prepares the reader for the actual explanation?

pages.title: Explain the proposed interaction.
pages.lead: A context card brings together a saved passage, the question that prompted it and a note about where it might be useful next.
pages.body: The proposed workflow is capture, connect and revisit. Explain those steps as a design direction. Do not describe integrations, collaboration, security or offline operation as shipped features.
pages.detail: Fold Notes explores a simple question: could preserving the reason for a note make later review more meaningful? A concept review should test that question.
pages.question: Which part requires an actual demonstration before publication?

pages.title: Keep proof beside the claim.
pages.lead: The phrase designed to preserve context describes an intention. The phrase improves recall would describe an outcome and needs different evidence.
pages.body: Maintain a claim register before publishing. Mark the concept statements as illustrative and outcome claims as unsupported. Copy approval is not scientific validation or permission to reuse someone else’s material.
pages.detail: Use the supplied source register as an authored exercise. Replace it only after checking the relevant product, evidence and rights information.
pages.question: What would a reasonable reader believe this sentence proves?

pages.title: Adapt meaning to the channel.
pages.lead: Email: A saved note can lose its question. Explore the Fold Notes concept. Social: Keep the thought beside the note. Read the concept outline.
pages.body: Landing-page copy has room to explain capture, connect and revisit. Neither short form should omit the concept status when that omission changes the reader’s understanding.
pages.detail: These are proposed copy routes, not sent messages. The channel register contains three planned placements with no delivery or audience measurements.
pages.question: What must remain visible even in the shortest version?

pages.title: Make the next action honest.
pages.lead: Review the concept outline is more accurate than start now when no working product or public destination has been established.
pages.body: Match the action to a real destination before release. Describe any requested information and its purpose. Do not imply enrolment, availability or a promised reply without an operational basis.
pages.detail: A button label is not a functioning service. Verify the destination, accessible name, form behaviour and privacy notice in the actual publishing environment.
pages.question: Can the destination fulfil exactly what the action promises?

pages.title: Review the release as a system.
pages.lead: Read the headline, description, qualification and next action together. A correct disclaimer cannot repair a misleading headline that the reader sees first.
pages.body: Assign product, editorial and rights review separately. The source register leaves all three placements at draft status. No reviewer or release authority has been appointed by this example.
pages.detail: Check accessible text, image rights and destination behaviour alongside the message. A completed checklist records a review; it does not certify compliance.
pages.question: Which unresolved gate should stop publication?

records.label: Editorial gate
records.prompt: Meaning is consistent across the three placements.

records.label: Product gate
records.prompt: Capability language matches an inspectable artifact.

records.label: Rights gate
records.prompt: Use and distribution permissions are checked.

evidenceRows: 3 proposed placements; no sends or results supplied.

pages.title: Learn without inventing a launch result.
pages.lead: After a real release, compare the observed reader response with the explanation task. Start with what was actually delivered and which destinations were available.
pages.body: This template has no impressions, sends, clicks or conversions. Record denominators, time windows and consent conditions before reporting rates. Separate a reader’s confusion from a product-quality conclusion.
pages.detail: Carry forward the clearest unresolved question. Revise the message when its meaning fails; do not treat an untested headline choice as a measured winner.
pages.question: What evidence would justify keeping or changing the message?
